problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a circuit for a specialized freight vehicle that is required to stop at 13 distinct distribution hubs:

Hub Beta: Positioned at grid reference (5,43)
Hub Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (190,175)

Hub Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (183,20)

Hub Lambda: Positioned at grid reference (10,64)
Hub Mu: Positioned at grid reference (87,188)

Due to infrastructural limitations, no direct transport link exists between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta.
Furthermore, owing to scheduling and regulatory constraints, the planned circuit must incorporate exactly one of the following two critical corridors: the link between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the link between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every hub precisely one time before returning to the point of origin.
